Package com.github.crittscott.somestacks.gametest

Class RenderOverrideChecks

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somestacks.gametest.RenderOverrideChecks
public final class RenderOverrideChecks extends Object
The client's own render-override file, config/somestacks/item_overrides.json, driven through the handlers /ss item and /ss write changed call. They need no client singleton, so they run headlessly against the real file, which each check backs up and restores.

  • Method Details

    • userFileIsNeverOverwrittenWhenUnreadableAndKeepsMalformedEntries

      public static void userFileIsNeverOverwrittenWhenUnreadableAndKeepsMalformedEntries(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      To reproduce in-game: quit, put a syntax error in config/somestacks/item_overrides.json (delete its last closing brace), start the game, and run /ss item minecraft:apple gui and then /ss write changed. The command fails, saying the file could not be read, and the file is unchanged. Restore the brace, add "minecraft:dirt": {"mode": "flat"}, and run /ss write changed again: it succeeds, the file gains the apple entry, and it keeps the dirt entry exactly as written along with every other entry. Then run /ss item minecraft:dirt reset and /ss write changed: the dirt entry is gone.

      The handlers' one-time read is reset by reflection before each scenario, standing in for a restart.

    • malformedFieldsKeepTheEntrysValidFields

      public static void malformedFieldsKeepTheEntrysValidFields(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      To reproduce in-game: in a resource pack's assets/minecraft/item_render_overrides/minecraft.json, give minecraft:apple {"mode": "gui", "scale": "big"} and minecraft:stick {"mode": "nope", "scale": 2}, then reload resources. The log warns about each bad field, the apple renders in gui mode at normal size, and the stick renders at double size with its measured mode.
